data.body: Operator 2026-09-29: 'Make ddflow to promote and recommend to the agent to execute the tests in the workflow as relevant and as parallel as possible'. Scope: (a) services/testselect.py: the tests relevant to a diff (base...HEAD plus the working tree): changed test files, tests importing a changed module or anything that transitively imports it (Python AST import graph over the repo), and tests named after a changed file's stem; each with its reason; (b) a parallel command to run them, derived from the configured unit_tests command (runner prefix + its options + the files), -n auto when xdist is declared; (c) 'ddflow tests [--item] [--base]' CLI + ddflow_tests MCP tool, following the pins shape; (d) the driver says: while implementing run 'ddflow tests' (relevant, parallel) after each change; the unit_tests gate runs the WHOLE suite, in parallel; (e) gate status for unit_tests names both; (f) leftovers from B-parallel-tests: doctor passes the repo root to the workflow check so the serial-pytest advisory shows there, and the init template / ddflow_configure text propose 'pytest -q -n auto'. data.body: Measured 2026-09-29 on the LAN critic (vLLM, ~35 generated tokens/s per request while serving two): 2371 chars 624 s, 5436 chars 1133 s, 8190 empty completion, 30000 timeout; reasoning_effort low / enable_thinking false come back off contract. So a 44k-char diff is ~9 sequential chunks x ~1000 s = ~2.5 h. vLLM batches concurrent requests, so aggregate throughput rises with concurrency while per-request speed drops far less. (a) [[reviewer]].max_concurrency (default 1 = today) runs up to N chunks at once, results assembled in chunk order; (b) total_budget_s applies to the wall clock, not the sum; (c) partial/unavailable accounting unchanged per chunk. Measure before/after on a real diff.

data.body: Bug Bd5b59f3894: _memory_sources accepts any source containing '/' as a path; a lesson seen_in that is a sentence reaches (repo/rel).is_file() and raises OSError Errno 36 in run_nemo_run, so verify never ran there. Fix: a source is a path only if it is one path-shaped token (no whitespace, bounded length); and a stat that raises OSError is 'not a path', never a crash or a vanished finding. Regression test: an imported lesson whose seen_in is a >255-char sentence with '/' -- verify_import returns a report; fails on current code with OSError.
data.title: import --verify never crashes on an imported record whose source is prose, not a path (fixes bug Bd5b59f3894)

data.body: Bug B259fd32dbd: enforce.installed only finds HOOK_MARKER in .git/hooks/<name>; a pre-commit-framework hook never carries it, so run_nemo_run (ddflow-check-commit / ddflow-check-msg local hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml) is told 'NOT installed ... NOTHING checks it' and exit 2. Fix: a framework-generated hook (the 'File generated by pre-commit' header) whose .pre-commit-config.yaml has a hook at that stage whose entry runs 'hooks check-commit' / 'hooks check-msg' counts as installed, and status says it is armed through pre-commit. Regression test: repo with such a config + generated hooks -> status reports both installed, exit 0; fails on current code.
data.title: hooks status recognises ddflow checks armed through the pre-commit framework (fixes bug B259fd32dbd)

data.body: Bug B438d336b24: 'Phase: NOPE.99' passes check-msg. Fix: the value of an item_trailer_keys trailer must be the id of an item in the queue (not removed); new [enforce].trailer_waivers = {key = [words]} declares keys that mark a commit shipping no item (run_nemo_run: Phase-ships = none|filing|recon|evidence|followup), whose value must be one of those words. A queue that cannot be read is exit 2 (could not run), never a pass. run_nemo_run's config gets the waiver map in the same change window. Regression test: NOPE.99 refused naming the key and value; a real id passes; Phase-ships: none passes with the waiver, Phase-ships: bogus refused; fails on current code.
data.title: The item trailer must name an item in the queue; a waiver key takes only its declared words (fixes bug B438d336b24)

data.body: Bug B45d5aa72fa: the importer never completes a phase. With --include-done a phase whose every imported task is done/closed (or that has no tasks and whose heading carries the done marker) must be imported completed with evidence naming the source; a phase with open tasks stays open. Without --include-done, the report must say how many ticked tasks per phase were left out so '0/3' is not read as 'nothing shipped'. Also a re-run of --include-done over an existing import must add the missing done tasks under existing phases (103.A/103.C under 103). Regression test on a fixture with a CLOSED phase, a partly-shipped phase and an open one; fails on current code.
data.title: import --include-done completes a finished phase; a plain import says which ticked tasks it left out (fixes bug B45d5aa72fa)

Fix: optmem default=false with a why that points at ddflow memory; memory companion text current; registered_in also matches an entry whose command+args equal the companion's launch (and reports the name it is registered under). (a) Config.load: a key a config FILE carries that this code does not know is kept in cfg.unknown_knobs and skipped, not raised; (b) doctor reports each as a problem-level note ('unknown knob X in .ddflow/config.toml: a typo, or written by a newer ddflow -- merge main'), and config --explain lists them; (c) writers (config --set, --append-toml, workflow gate) stay strict: an unknown key is still refused at write time; (d) env vars unaffected; (e) re-enable local_files = ['.roborev.toml']. data.summary: check-commit's staged_paths runs 'git -C <primary> diff --cached' while git hands the hook the WORKTREE's GIT_INDEX_FILE, so it diffs the worktree index against the PRIMARY checkout's HEAD instead of the worktree's: every file master modified since the branch point is reported as staged (demonstrated in a scratch repo: master edits shared.txt, the worktree stages mine.txt, ddflow sees 'A mine.txt, M shared.txt'), and the branch's own already-committed changes too (run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.1 with nothing staged: '.ddflow/config.toml'). Under commit_without_lease=block a branch behind master is refused for files it never touched; under warn it gets false warnings. Fix: run the staged diff in the tree being committed (_this_worktree), not the resolved primary.

data.body: Bug Bba366d9893: staged_paths(repo) runs git -C <primary> diff --cached with the hook's GIT_INDEX_FILE (the worktree's index), comparing it to the primary's HEAD: files master changed since the branch point and the branch's own committed changes read as staged. Fix: every staged-path read in the commit hooks (check_commit, check_views, check_docs and any other staged_paths caller) runs in the tree being committed (_this_worktree / cwd) with that tree's HEAD. Regression test: primary + worktree; master modifies shared.txt after the branch point; the worktree stages only mine.txt under a lease covering mine.txt; with commit_without_lease=block and GIT_INDEX_FILE set as git sets it, check_commit returns 0 and staged_paths is exactly [mine.txt]; fails on current code. Blocks run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.2 (block).
data.title: check-commit diffs the index against the committing worktree's HEAD, not the primary's (fixes bug Bba366d9893)

data.summary: The evidence contract is vacuous on every surface: api/gates.record adds the MEASURED tree_sha and diff_stat to the evidence dict before G.record checks 'a gate in gates.evidence_required needs evidence to pass', so the dict is never empty and a bare 'gate record <id> <gate> --outcome passed' with no note, command or output is accepted for unit_tests, rubber_duck, critic, standards (and docs). Probe: init, phase add P1, 'ddflow gate record P1 docs --outcome passed' -> exit 0. The check must look at what the CALLER supplied (note/command/output/model), not the measured fields.

data.body: Found while adding the docs phase gate (B-docs-phase-gate): api/gates.record sets tree_sha and diff_stat before services.gates.record checks evidence, so 'not evidence' is never true and gates.evidence_required is enforced nowhere through the CLI or MCP. Regression test: a bare passed on an evidence-required gate exits non-zero; with --evidence it passes; the measured fields are still recorded.
data.title: Evidence-required gates refuse a bare pass again: judge the caller's evidence (note, command, output, model), not the fields ddflow measures itself (fixes the vacuous-evidence bug)

data.how: Template: pid=$!; end=$((SECONDS+3600)); while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null && [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do sleep 30; done. Keep output files in a per-agent scratch subfolder. Before reporting, list your background shells and stop any still running.
data.rule: Every background 'wait until done' loop has (1) a deadline (e.g. SECONDS-based, exit non-zero when hit), (2) a condition that fails when the watched process DIES, not only a marker the process writes on a clean exit (check the PID with kill -0, or pair the marker test with it), (3) no 'pgrep -f <text>' whose text is in the loop's own command line, and (4) is stopped (TaskStop / kill) before the agent hands back.
data.summary: Background wait loops need a deadline and a liveness check (not just a clean-exit marker), must never pgrep -f a string in their own command, and must be stopped before the agent reports; otherwise they poll for hours after the work is gone.
data.title: A background wait loop must end by itself: a deadline, a liveness check, and stopped before the agent reports
data.why: 2026-09-30: six polling loops ran 5-21 hours after their agents had finished: they waited for EXIT=/FINISHED lines that reviews never wrote because the reviews hung (LAN Qwen), were cancelled, or had their output file overwritten in a shared scratchpad; one 'while pgrep -f "B-fix-declared-family-refute"' matched its own shell and could never end. They cost little CPU but made the task panel show phantom running work for a day.
